title: Backcasting from 'Eval Results Are Comparable Across Institutes': Reproducing One Eval Two Ways

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Eval Results Are Comparable Across Institutes': Reproducing One Eval Two Ways

**Problem:** A success state where international AI safety institutes can mutually recognize each other's evaluations requires that the same eval yield comparable results across implementations. Tiny differences in scaffolding, scoring, and prompts can make 'the same benchmark' produce divergent numbers, blocking mutual recognition.

**Direction:** Take one public safety/capability eval with an available reference implementation, then independently re-implement its scoring/scaffolding from the paper description and run both on the same small open model. Quantify the gap between the reference and the independent re-implementation, and isolate which under-specified choices (parsing, scoring tolerance, prompt template) drive divergence.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'cross-institute mutual recognition' shows implementation-reproducibility as the precondition. Demonstrating how much a faithful re-implementation diverges is a concrete argument for stricter eval specification standards in the International Network of AI Safety Institutes. Needs one small open model and public eval code — clean outsider experiment.

**Relevant context:** International Network of AI Safety Institutes seeks shared eval methodology; 'How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?' (arXiv:2601.23112) on verbatim versioning of prompts/rubrics; Inspect/lm-eval-harness ecosystems for reference implementations.
